#1981. Rabiot grateful for Amorim’s trust and offers insight into renewal plea: “Makes us feel important”

Speaking to French TV, Adrien Rabiot has looked at the interest from Ruben Amorim in a renewal at AC Milan and praised the Portuguese.

It’s no secret that Rabiot is one of Milan’s most important players. Gerry Cardinale admitted that he’s something of a ‘franchise player’ already and the love from Amorim has not been kept quiet. Indeed, the former Manchester United head coach is a huge admirer of his.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a summer of questions about his future, a renewal has seemed to be on the cards for the majority of the season and with continued good performances, the talk of one coming soon won’t go away. In fact, it could be completed before Christmas, with a deal reportedly close.

Speaking to Telefoot during the international break, Rabiot revealed a little more about his renewal and Amorim’s dream to offer him a new deal quickly into his tenure, as MilanNews have relayed.

“My excellent start to the season with good stats? It’s also positive to have players capable of being decisive without being attackers. It also encourages those around us. At Milan we have quite young players and it’s important for them to have role models in their everyday lives.

“I had been back from vacation for a week and he was already talking to me about a contract renewal. I told him: ‘Coach, calm down’ [he laughs]. But obviously, it’s important for a player to have this trust. The coach is counting on us; he has a high regard for us and makes us feel important.”

#1979. Křetínský’s Silence Is Becoming A Problem For West Ham

I think we’ve reached a point now where we need some more clarity from West Ham United about the future direction of the football club. Whilst I understand there is an overriding desire to get the Hammers promoted, something which has been described to us by club insiders as a priority, I’m increasingly concerned about how we intend to achieve it.

Because as things stand at the moment, West Ham appear rudderless. In fact, I’d go as far as to say we’re listing. We’re getting progressively worse, and there is a worrying lack of direction at the football club.

Whilst there may be a desire to reach a certain destination, I see very little from West Ham at the moment to suggest that we know the route. And that’s why I believe we really need to hear from Daniel Křetínský.

We’ve waited an awfully long time for the restructuring of West Ham’s shareholding to go through. And whilst Claret & Hugh reported earlier this month that the transactions had been completed, we’re still waiting for public confirmation from the football club.

Křetínský himself has indicated that he will engage with supporters once the share transaction has been finalised, but quite frankly, I don’t think that’s good enough anymore.

West Ham are in desperate need of leadership. Whatever the situation with his shareholding, Křetínský is already in a position of authority at the football club.

West Ham are still waiting for Daniel Kretinsky to address supporters

Whilst I don’t expect him to be shooting from the lip in the way David Sullivan used to, I do think he needs to provide some leadership, some direction and some communication with supporters as to what the actual plan is here.

Because almost everybody at every level of the football club, from the players right up to the very top, appears to be struggling.

Ideally, I’d like to know what the direction of travel is. What is the plan for West Ham United?

They want to take us forward, but how are they going to do that? What’s the plan for January? What’s the plan for investment?

We sold around £200m worth of players during the summer, we’ve yet to see the anticipated injection of funds from the shareholders, and we currently don’t look anything like a team capable of mounting a successful promotion challenge.

And that, by the club’s own admission, is supposed to be the number one priority.

As things stand, the team are getting worse and the club appear to be getting worse. I don’t think West Ham supporters are being unreasonable in wanting to know what the people running our football club intend to do about it.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

I suggest looking at another club owned by Kretinsky, Sparta Prague. They are in very deep crisis at this moment, appointing interim coach from 3rd league (for context 3rd Czech league is semi-professional). Several key figures from club leadership has left together with previous coach. Following how the things will unfold there, in a club with his sole ownership, can be a lead on what may happen in West Ham should the things go on similar trajectory.

Kretinsky has us following a similar model to BS . Getting people in that you’ve worked with before not qualified people. Look at what has happened to Sparta Prague since he took over. Historically the best team there but have now been usurped by their bitter city rivals. He kept Nuno in his job after he got us relegated. And whilst I am not asking for Parker to be sacked as he needs a few months at least in the job to try to turn things around. But long term I don’t think he will be good and he is of a similar type to our last 3 failed managers which is what many of us fans no longer wanted………

I get that people, and I include you in that Gonzo, dislike DK. You’ve been dangled the fruit of Staveley but I don’t think they’d be any better – at least its actually DKs money and not a group in the shadow only interested in profit.

I agree we seem rudderless. I’m not sure why you’d suspect a statement to actually benefit anything. It’d just be noise. The focus needs to be on fixing the issues behind the scenes.

I dont want it come out how much or how little they plan on investing, I don’t want them to tell us stories on training grounds and stadiums, because frankly that direction changes if we don’t go up.

Everyone at the club needs to be focused on that. Wait until February. Then let’s see where the lie of the land is. If there’s no investment, I’ll be standing with the pitchforks demanding DK leaves our club. But until then, we need to trust that behind the scenes things are being fixed. Unless you’ve heard that DK isn’t interested. Then id be concerned.

don’t need to know their plans for January, why would you show your hand and tell everyone how much money you have, sounds like Andy Burnham negotiating skills… there will be a plan, even if it’s not working yet. They wouldn’t have persuaded Bowen,Soucek and Maverpanos etc to stay if there wasn’t. But having a plan in football doesn’t always go your way, that’s why the best clubs need time.

Not sure I agree. GSB were very vocal about their plans for West Ham and look where they ended up.

Clubs whose owners start spouting about vision, direction and aims tend to end up with egg on their face (very much like governments and politicians) so I much prefer the quiet approach that Kretinsky is well known for.

#1978. Number of times 2025-26 Premier League clubs each selected by the broadcasters, facility fees

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Interesting to see which Premier League clubs featured the most when it came to UK broadcasters selecting their matches across the 2025-26 league season, plus how it impacted on facility fees.

The information made public via the publication of the EPL’s official 2025-26 annual report.

This report included a breakdown of how much money each of last season’s 20 Premier League clubs banked.

In total, the 20 Premier League clubs received £3,142m for the 2025-26 season, this was a 10.9% increase on the 2024-25 season.

Banking the most were Arsenal with £198.1m, whilst Wolves received the least with £117.2m. The Premier League is actually one of the very fairest major European leagues in terms of the gap between which clubs get the very most and very least. Arsenal getting 1.69 x what Wolves received.

This is how many times each of the 20 Premier League clubs were shown live in the UK across the 2025/26 Premier League season:

34 Man U, Aston Villa, Forest 33 Arsenal 32 Man City 31 Newcastle United, Liverpool, Chelsea, Spurs 30 Crystal Palace 28 Leeds 26 Fulham, Everton 25 Brentford, West Ham 23 Bournemouth 22 Sunderland 21 Wolves 20 Brighton 17 Burnley

The facilities fees portion of the Premier League share out each season is overwhelmingly based on how many times each of the Premier League clubs were chosen for UK TV.

So last season Manchester United finished third in the 2025-26 Premier League table but received more in facilities fees (£24.om) cash than title winners Arsenal (£23.3m), Man U having 34 matches shown live by UK TV and Arsenal 33.

Wolves finished 20th last season with Burnley 19th, yet Wolves got £13.9m in facilities fees compared to the £11.5m that Burnley got, due to Wolves picked 21 times for UK live TV and Burnley only 17.

Sunderland finished five places above Newcastle United in the Premier League table (7th and 12th) but Newcastle got  £20.3m in facilities fees and Sunderland only £15.5m. TV chiefs showing Newcastle 31 times and Sunderland on only 22 occasions.

The number of times clubs are shown on UK Live TV is now significantly impacted for some clubs if they are in the Europa League or Conference League. Every Premier League match is now automatically shown on TV in the UK if not a 3pm Saturday game. The new TV deal saw that implemented from the 2025-26 season onwards and even if TNT Sports or Sky Sports didn’t originally select them, all the Premier League matches moved due to clubs’ Europa League or Conference League games are automatically shown on Sky Sports. This played a major part in both Villa And Forest shown 34 times of 38 Premier League matches last season on UK TV. So clubs such as Sunderland and Bournemouth are all but guaranteed to be shown more times in the 2026-27 season on UK TV than they were in 2025-26.

For Newcastle United so far this season, nine of the eleven Premier League matches that have been played have been shown live on UK TV, the exceptions Hull at home and Fulham away. The selections have now been made until the end of January 2027 by Sky and TNT, of these next 12 EPL rounds of games another nine Newcastle United matches are scheduled to be shown by UK broadcasters, that will mean after 23 Premier League games for Newcastle United, 18 of the 23 will have been shown. The upcoming exceptions are Ipswich away in December and then the home games against Fulham and Brighton in late January 2027.

As an illustration of the overall breakdown for a club, Newcastle United received a total of £153.7m in the 2025-26 Premier League cash share out and this was broken down as:

UNITED KINGDOM (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £31.9m Facility Fees £20.3m Merit £15.4m

OVERSEAS (VIA THE TV DEALS ETC.) Equal Share £56.5m Merit £18.4m

#1977. Yasir Al-Rumayyan explaining why Saudi Arabia PIF bought Newcastle United

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Saudi Arabia PIF Governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan flew in for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal.

As always though, when Yasir Al-Rumayyan is part of a PIF visiting group to Tyneside, it also sparks intrigue as to other potential reasons for his/their visit.

On Wednesday, an exclusive from The Athletic reported that the Newcastle United owners were now planning to sell a stake in the club that would enable a new party (or parties) to own 25% of NUFC.

The report stating that this would be done by issuing new shares.

So if a 25% share in the club was sold via the issue of new shares, the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reuben family (Chris Waugh at The Athletic has on Thursday confirmed that they as well as PIF would see their shareholding diluted) would see their ownership of the club reduce respectively from 84% to 63% and 16% to 12%.

The Athletic reporting on Wednesday that the idea with selling the 25% stake in NUFC is not for any money to go directly to PIF or the Reubens, instead it is intended that the money generated by selling a quarter ownership of the club would be put towards spending on the infrastructure, the state of the art training ground and a new stadium. With estimates of a club current valuation now of up to £2billion, that would potentially mean up to £500million raised towards financing the new Newcastle United stadium and training ground.

Unsurprisingly this sparked a lot of conjecture in the media and amongst fans.

Was the Yasir Al-Rumayyan visit to Tyneside not simply to watch the Arsenal match and indeed, what did The Athletic exclusive potentially suggest about future plans of the Saudi Arabia PIF majority ownership?

I think what is key is to go back and revisit exactly why PIF bought a controlling stake in Newcastle United.

This below is Yasir Al-Rumayyan handily explaining himself why the Saudi Arabia PIF bought the majority ownership of the club.

Yasir Al-Rumayyan speaking on 4 October 2022, a few days before the first anniversary of the Newcastle United takeover:

“We bought the whole team (Newcastle United) for £350m, instead of only having 30 per cent in another team (Manchester United) for £700m.

“You can see Chelsea was sold for $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

“So, my potential now is to go from £350m to at least $3.5bn (£2.5bn).

“Football of course is one of the most important sports there is, whether domestically (in Saudi Arabia) or abroad.

“It is the number one sport in the world and why the English Premier League?

“Well, because it is the best league in the world, no other league competes with it.

“There are 20 teams, three are relegated, three are promoted, the advantage of the Premier League is that any of the 20 teams can beat the best team in the league.

“When we looked at it, we looked at it from a financial perspective.

“By the way, it wasn’t the first offer we got regarding a football team. We looked in Italy, France and the UK as well.

“In the UK there was a team (Manchester United) that approached us on the basis that we take 30 per cent of the ownership and (on the condition that) we don’t interfere at all in terms of managing the club, for £700m.

“Then we bought Newcastle, who offered us 100 per cent of the ownership, but Amanda Staveley and her husband who got us the opportunity told us, ‘We like it so much, we would like to be with you’….and that was perfect.

“Then came the Reuben family, who are one of the biggest property investors (in the UK), saying that, ‘We would like to come with you’, and these are one of the biggest investors in (the City of) Newcastle (Upon Tyne).

“I said, ‘Perfect! Tell them to come’. So now they (Amanda Staveley, her husband and the Reubens) have a skin in the game.”

Just under five months later, Amanda Staveley was speaking at the FT Business of Football Summit in Mayfair, London on Thursday 2 March 2023 and she then gave further insight into why the Saudi Arabia PIF had decided to buy Newcastle United:

“When we walked into a Newcastle United game we said why spend X Billion when you can spend three hundred and some million and put in….I think we have put in two hundred plus to date of new money since we bought the club.

“We had a particular business plan, based on a five, ten, fifteen year timeline.

“Critical to that plan was making sure we had the right partners.

“So making sure (Saudi Arabia) PIF, who are very long-term investors.

“Hoping potentially there might be the chance of Champions League.

“I love the valuations that are reflecting in Chelsea….because it makes our valuation look very compelling.

“We bought the club at under two times revenue.

“When you are looking at five to seven times revenue, that is a lot of money.”

What was said by Yasir Al-Rumayyan just over four years ago (and then Amanda Staveley just over three and a half years ago) very much fits in with what is happening now, in my opinion. Their prediction/expectation of huge growth in the value of Newcastle United has become reality and now further steps to be taken in order to help push that valuation far far higher. Part of that plan appears to now be to bring in money from other investors which will help to finance essential infrastructure projects, namely the stadium and training ground. Injecting cash from elsewhere via an issue of new shares that then reduces the levels of money that may then needed to be loaned to help cover the spending, plus it also reduces the exposure of the Saudi Arabia PIF and the Reubens.

#1976. West Ham Must Use Souček Or Risk Losing Him

Following the news that Tomáš Souček has the opportunity to leave West Ham for a Premier League club in January, I have to say that I’m becoming extremely worried about the direction of the football club.

Claret & Hugh spoke to one of Souček’s representatives earlier today, and whilst they made it clear that his preference was to help fire West Ham back into the Premier League, it’s clear that he is a man in demand.

One Premier League club in particular is understood to be surprised that Souček has not been playing more frequently for West Ham and, as a result, is happy to test the water to discover whether he’s surplus to requirements at the London Stadium.

In my opinion, this is not something West Ham should consider, not for a moment.

Even before this news, I was going to put forward my case for Souček being involved from the start against Stoke City.

He’s consistently posed a threat off the bench, not least during last night’s defeat at Portsmouth, and has scored three goals as a substitute this season.

In the absence of any sort of goalscoring form from our strikers, Souček would seem like one of the most likely sources of goals in a team which has gone from being free-scoring and among the top goalscorers in the division to one that struggles to do anything other than hit the woodwork.

A lot has been made about West Ham having Premier League players, but I’m not sure how many of them truly are. Souček, however, very firmly falls into that category.

He’s a European trophy winner, an international player, a proven Premier League goalscorer and more than capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

This is a player who signed a new West Ham contract only last month and whose commitment to the football club has never really been in question.

But what has just become abundantly clear is that if we don’t use him, we’re likely to lose him.

And I find it highly unlikely that West Ham will be able to bring in a better player than Tomáš Souček in the January transfer window.

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Fabian Hurzeler and Brighton host Matthias Jaissle and his Newcastle United team on Sunday in the Premier League.

However, the Seagulls have a match to play before they face Newcastle United.

Whilst Fabian Hurzeler insists that this next match is the only important one he is giving focus to at this moment in time,  his actions suggest otherwise.

Fabian Hurzeler is also tonight leaving out Olivier Boscagli who has been ill and Jaouen Hadjam who has had a minor knock, but both like Diego Gomez set to be involved against Newcastle United if selected.

It shouldn’t do Newcastle United any harm the fact that Brighton have this extra game to play, at the same time though, the demands of a Premier League club also competing in the third level UEFA competition are a little different to trying to cope with the Champions League as well as the Premier League schedule.

Brighton’s top player this season has been Pascal Gross and he could also be rested against the Romanian side tonight and kept for Newcastle United. With Fabian Hurzeler stating that he will rely on his “very trustful relationship” with Pascal Gross as to whether the midfielder will be up to the challenge of starting both matches.

Hurzeler revealed that Malik Yalcouye is out now for up to 10 weeks and misses both tonight and the Newcastle United match.

Joao Costinha is another who will definitely miss out against the Magpies, he is suspended after having been sent off during the 20 defeat at Hull City last weekend.

Kaoru Mitoma (knee), Stefanos Tzimas (thigh), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh) are also set to be missing for both of these upcoming matches.

However, Femi Azeez could be back from a thigh injury tonight, though whether he would be able to cope with playing against both Universitatea Craiova and Newcastle United is an unknown.

#1974. Newcastle United struggles can be summed up by one word

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Under Eddie Howe, Newcastle United had a clear identity.

That was to be a pressing machine, giving teams no time to breathe at times and overrun them in midfield, thanks to physical players such as Tonali and Joelinton.

That was the expectation, almost a demand of the Newcastle United fans, as a Wor flags banner read ‘Get into them’.

Four months on though from Eddie Howe’s departure,  a clear sense of identity is yet to be implemented by Matthias Jaissle.

Jaissle arrived as an unknown to the Premier League, having arrived from Al-Ahli, it has not been smooth sailing so far.

As a club that qualified for the Champions League 18 months ago, is a mid-table finish expected this time around?

It must be stated that this is not the same Newcastle United team that finished top five and qualified for the Champions League in the 2024-25 season.

Having lost the likes of Bruno Guimaraes and Alexander Isak, to Premier League rivals Arsenal and Liverpool respectively. They have lost huge presences in the team and currently lack a talisman to influence a game as well as players such as Isak and Bruno G did multiple times.

Diving deeper, an argument can be made that Newcastle have not hit the same heights since the departure of Alexander Isak in 2025.

Late summer 2025 signings Yoane Wissa and Nick Woltemade struggled for goals, scoring just 14 goals combined between them last season in all competitions. This compares to Isak’s 27 goals in his final Newcastle United season,

The 2025-26 season saw Newcastle United finish 12th in the Premier League, seven places below where they placed the year before and a massive 17 points worse off.

In my opinion the reasons for this can be summarised into two points, which are lack of away form and dropping points from winning positions. They won just four away games in the Premier League and dropped a crazy 30+ points from winning positions. This suggests Newcastle United have for some time not been the same team that did so well in 2024-25.

Matthias Jaissle officially became Newcastle United Head Coach only 18 days before the start of the season. This gave him little time to bring in players to fit his system of ‘vertical football’ and work his football philosophy into the current players before their first match against Liverpool.

I think it can be said that Newcastle United did start the season well, with three wins and two draws in their first five games (in all competitions).

After those opening five matches including a Premier League win over Spurs and draws against Liverpool and Bournemouth, I believed that Newcastle would be in a battle for the European places. However, wins have been hard to find. Also a defeat in the Carabao Cup at Everton.

One of the main reasons for the struggles has been the lack of goals from Osula and Wissa, just two between them.  Meanwhile out on loan, Nick Woltemade has scored five goals so far for Juventus.

Looking at the wider stats, in the Premier League against Coventry and Everton, Newcastle had 36 shots in total but only eight of those on target, scoring just one goal.

Also, new signings have struggled. Fernandez-Pardo without a goal so far, whilst players such as Toure and Bamba are yet to start a Premier League match.

I think Newcastle United’s struggles can currently be summed up in one word – change.

Change in manager with new ideas, a change in system still being perfected and big change in the squad with a lot of younger players being brought in who are still adapting to the physicality of the Premier League.

There is though definitely something to build on, the 2-2 draw with Arsenal gave fans hope.

To answer the question of what the goal for the rest of the season should be, I believe it should be the idea of identity and growth. Allowing Matthias Jaissle to work on his system, find his best team and use this season as a transitional one.

A big challenge will be the big home fixtures against Manchester United and Sunderland, we might know a lot more after these games.

#1973. Newcastle United identity, recruitment and putting things right

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

In your opinion, what are the key problems that Newcastle United face?

Not the greatest start to the season, so where has it all gone wrong compared to qualifying for the Champions League and winning the Carabao Cup in 2025?

After a poor 2025-26 season and the departures of Bruno Guimarães, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, the club needed to bring in proven replacements.

Instead, Newcastle United have signed young, unproven players. Bazoumana Touré, Aladji Bamba and others are not ready to replace players like Gordon and Tonali. There is also no guarantee that they will ever reach that level.

The summer recruitment simply wasn’t good enough.

Most Newcastle United fans still support Matthias Jaissle but there are concerns about the way the team is playing.

Some have criticised Jaissle’s tactics, he uses the Red Bull philosophy which is built around intense pressing, quick transitions, vertical attacks and athletic players. While this style can be effective, it is not always easy to get right.

Newcastle Unite need to find a way to make these tactics work with the players they have. In my opinion the performances have not been good enough, questions are starting to be asked.

Another major problem is the lack of experience in the Newcastle United squad, young players need time to develop.

When you are trying to compete in the Premier League you need experienced players in the here and now who can handle pressure and help the team through difficult periods.

Losing experienced players has left a big gap in the squad and Newcastle United need players who can make an immediate impact, not just players who might become good in a few years.

In my opinion, Newcastle United seem to have lost some of the identity that made them successful. The team used to play with energy, intensity and passion, difficult to play against.

Performances have become inconsistent, supporters need to see a team that fights for every ball and gives everything for the badge.

Newcastle United need to get their recruitment right, the club cannot overly rely on young players who are not ready to make an immediate difference.

They also need to find consistency under the manager. The tactics need to suit the players, the team needs to show the same energy and desire that made them successful in the past.

There is still time for Newcastle United to turn things around but changes need to happen soon.

#1972. West Ham Set For Double Blow Ahead Of Stoke City Clash

The London Stadium is a tough venue to fill for West Ham given its huge capacity, even when everything is going well. Therefore, there was always likely to be a reduced attendance against Stoke City on Saturday anyway, given the Hammers’ recent performances and results.

But it looks set to get considerably worse, with many of those using public transport to get to the stadium facing significant disruption.

A number of railway engineering works are scheduled for the weekend of 28-29 November, coinciding with West Ham’s 3pm Championship kick-off against the in-form Potters. Supporters travelling from Essex in particular will need to allow additional time for their journeys.

Essex and Shenfield: National Rail has confirmed disruption to Greater Anglia services, with replacement buses connecting passengers to the Central line at Newbury Park.

Lea Bridge: Engineering works mean Hertford East services normally terminating at Stratford will be diverted to Liverpool Street. There will also be no trains between Meridian Water and Stratford.

There will be no Elizabeth line services through central London due to additional engineering works, although Stratford station itself remains open.

Supporters can also consult West Ham’s official stadium travel guide, which includes information on accessible shuttle buses.

Given the growing frustration amongst West Ham supporters, I wouldn’t be at all surprised if the travel hassle caused by the trains is enough to dissuade the 50/50s from attending the London Stadium. As a result, I’d expect a lot of empty seats on Saturday.

For all those attending, please ensure you check travel before leaving.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#1971. GdS: ‘Plays, scores and has fun’ – Pulisic the star in a Milan team rivalling the greats

Last night, AC Milan added another five goals to their tally in Serie A, making it one of their best starts to a season ever.

With Ruben Amorim, Milan are no longer the defence-first team that Massimiliano Allegri made them. Instead, they’re fluid, attacking and dangerous and the statistics show as much. So much so that their stars are shining brighter than they may have ever done before.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are on fire, so much so that they’ve only outscored this season’s start twice in their history. With 28 goals in 12 games, everyone is helping things tick, but Pulisic, again, is standing out.

After a fine international break, the American ‘led the way’ again and added a goal to his tally for the season in fine fashion. He dons the superhero cape in a team that ‘plays, scores and has fun’ and with him, the team keep winning.

Every 87 minutes in the league, he’s contributed and for that reason, there’s a sense of inevitability seeing him in the teamsheet. Gazzetta writes that it’s effectively like entering every game with a 1-0 lead already.

He’s now scored in three consecutive games and it’s form that has not been bettered since the start of the 2024/25 season; where he scored four goals in a row. It’s not really a surprise, either.

In Ruben Amorim’s front-foot system, he’s one of the frontmen and that naturally means he’s going to score and create more. A ‘perfect match’ for Amorim, he’s leading in every sense and you’d have to look to the teams of Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler for more goals – both teams scored 29 in their first 12 games of the Serie A season.

Ardon Jashari grabbing a goal also raised the number of scorers this season to eight, which is impressive in itself. It’s a ‘super-attacking’ team where everyone contributes, but Pulisic is again leading.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

#1970. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#1968. West Ham Target January Move For Arsenal Wonderkid

West Ham United are reportedly preparing a January loan move for highly rated Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri as Scott Parker looks to strengthen his squad for the second half of the Championship season.

According to an exclusive from Steve Kay at FootballTransfers, the Hammers have revived their interest in the 19-year-old attacking midfielder, having previously targeted him under Nuno Espírito Santo.

Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund, having joined the German club on a season-long deal in September. However, the youngster has played just 29 minutes across Dortmund’s last seven matches, and Arsenal could consider recalling him before sending him elsewhere.

Having the ability to operate both centrally and on the right wing, Nwaneri could offer Parker some much-needed attacking options.

Ethan Nwaneri has been linked with a move to West Ham

Personally, I would absolutely welcome Nwaneri to West Ham. If nothing else, it could free up Jarrod Bowen to play more centrally.

Clearly, the West Ham captain has lost at least a yard of pace and is struggling stuck out on the right wing. I can’t quite shift from my mind his wonderful second-half performance against Cardiff City, when he was given something of a free role.

Unfortunately, Parker has since reverted to using Bowen as a conventional right winger, and we’re once again struggling to get the best out of our captain.

Whether anything comes of the Nwaneri link remains to be seen, particularly given the complications surrounding his existing loan agreement.

Personally, I think West Ham could do with improving both wings in the January transfer window. And that’s really just the tip of the iceberg for a team that needs serious surgery.

If you thought things couldn’t get any worse for West Ham, they certainly did last night, with the club dropping down to 13th in the EFL Championship. Four games took place on Wednesday evening, and the results made pretty grim reading for Hammers fans.

The Hammers are already 11 points adrift of the automatic promotion places and eight behind West Brom.

With rampant Stoke City next up for Scott Parker’s team at the London Stadium on Saturday, things aren’t getting any easier. We’re going to have to start winning games just to prevent what is already becoming quite a sizeable gap from getting any bigger.

#1966. Rabiot stars, Ramos scores: Fan player ratings for Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan treated fans in San Siro and across the world to a dominant display on Sunday night, as they beat Frosinone 5-1.

In recent seasons, a significant win against the visitors may have gone under the radar. However, Milan picked apart a side that was in the European places before the start of this weekend’s action. It’s a huge result.

Of course, the opposition’s playing style helped the Rossoneri a little bit; that can’t be denied. Yet, they hardly rolled over and still threatened to take something from the game before the scoreline became so wide.

As you’d expect, our own ratings were really high, with no one scoring below a 6/10 and Adrien Rabiot was given the Man of the Match award. The consensus from you, the readers who voted after full-time, was also that all of the players were really solid.

Scoring 0.4 higher than he did in our ratings, Rabiot was again seen as the MOTM and it’s understandable why. Then, Luka Modric followed with a 7.8 and Christian Pulisic scored a 7.6 to round up the top three. With his goal, Goncalo Ramos scored a 7.3, which is his highest rating from your scores so far. Perhaps he’d have scored even higher if he’d stayed on.

On the lower end of the scale, Davide Bartesaghi was the only starter given below a 6/10, whilst Omari Hutchinson (5.7) and Pervis Estupinan (5.4) were not viewed as impressive from the bench. Nevertheless, it’s a high average for the team.

#1965. Footy Headlines: Puma to deliver ‘pure and traditional’ final home shirt for Milan in 2027-28

The recent talk about AC Milan and kits has involved Adidas and a report has taken us back a year to Puma’s final shirt.

Next year, Puma will release their final home shirt for Milan, ending a 10-year stint as the club’s technical partner. It’s been an up-and-down period for the Rossoneri, but their return to Adidas will hopefully help to bring around more consistent, better times.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent update, Footy Headlines have provided ‘practically a final look’ at next season’s kit, which will mark the end of the Puma era. Provided to them by kit insider JMFK, the new shirt is expected to feature a polo collar and the classic Rossoneri stripes, as you’d expect.

The German brand are expected to embrace a ‘pure, traditional approach’ across the whole set, rather than being experimental with wild graphics. There’ll be no gradients, patterns or overcomplicated gimmicks, so it should be simple red and black stripes.

With thinner stripes than the current home shirt – modelled on the 1998-99 Scudetto shirt – it’ll also feature a collar for the first time since the 2018-19 season.

With this set to be the last home shirt before the return to Adidas, it certainly does Puma a lot of credit and it will hopefully round off the 10-year stint in style.

#1964. Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

Christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a new contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be said, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”

The big issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

The Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under new boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

#1963. Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino issues Luke Shaw fitness update as "fragile" accusation is rejected

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:12

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to confirm whether Luke Shaw will be involved in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has made the trip to Portugal alongside his teammates, having recovered from the muscular problem that has sidelined him since the early stages of October.

The 31-year-old has been a huge miss at the back for Man United, and Pochettino has welcomed the Englishman's return to fitness.

However, it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Sporting.

“All the players need to feel they can have an impact for the team and they can perform," Pochettino told reporters during his pre-game press conference.

“It’s up to us to give the opportunities to every single player in the moment that we believe that they deserve to be involved in the game.

“Of course, I know Luke from the past, in our time in Southampton, but all [of us who are] involved, we are not the same people now. It’s more than 10 years ago.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form.

“It’s good to have him, because he’s experienced everything with the squad, but we’ll see if he can be involved tomorrow or not, from the beginning or during the game.”

Matheus Cunha is suspended for the match following his red card against Roma in the team's last European fixture, while Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are all injured for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino also insisted during his press conference that Man United are 'not a fragile team' despite their huge difficulties this season.

The Red Devils will enter the game with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, and they currently sit down in 19th spot in the Premier League table.

"We are not fragile, we are a strong team who last season finished third. Sometimes things happen in football for different reasons. We need to identify why and we are working on it. I think we are going to turn the situation around," said the head coach.

Man United have two wins and two draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League, beating Sabah and Roma either side of defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como.
